version_decision.publication_policy: One coordinated public transition after qualification; no intermediate stable feature releases.

shared_representations.identity: Raw components and attachment-relative CatalogObjectRef; no local aliases, pointers or OIDs. Full identity in all caches.
shared_representations.values: TypedValueBatch preserving original Arrow metadata and typed NULLs. Option RESET differs from NULL and omission.
shared_representations.expressions: SqlExpression declares semantic profile and owner schema. No private AST/bound-plan serialization.
shared_representations.capabilities: Agreement scoped to sealed attachment state; validate per-object requirements and current write eligibility at execution.
shared_representations.mutation: Whole-operation validation, worker authority, coherent transactions and metadata/dependency updates. Durable operation identity is required for replay.
shared_representations.rollout: Use versioned endpoints/processes with draining; prove transaction/reconnect and downgrade behavior. The existing dispatcher cannot host two versions under one protocol name.
shared_representations.column_paths: Nine existing column RPCs use raw component paths, with per-operation nested DDL profiles and one-component 1.5 adapter targets. TableInfo.required_filters now uses AND-of-OR raw component paths across SDKs and the native 1.5 optimizer; native 2.0 integration remains open.

dependencies.title: Dependencies and catalog consistency

transactions.title: Transactions and write replay
scope: Explicit DDL rollback and mixed DDL/DML atomicity guarantees; operation identity/deduplication if retry support is included

Define ambiguous commit/reply-loss behavior; never retry side effects just because transport failed. No distributed atomicity claim across independent catalogs.

triggers.title: Triggers — design required
scope: Table-owned identity, list/get/create/drop and metadata mutation, event/timing/granularity, UPDATE OF, transition aliases, action definition, dependencies, and execution mode

Prefer worker authority for persistent definitions. Distinguish engine-executed from backend-executed triggers so they cannot fire twice. Define SQL dialect, ordering, supported row/statement forms, OLD/NEW requirements, rollback, detach/reconnect, and cross-client discovery.

query.title: Catalog query execution — existing design to consolidate
scope: Negotiated query preparation, typed parameters/context, prepared-result schema and lifetime, and execution through the existing TABLE stream

logical_types.title: Logical type preservation — design required
scope: Recursive type annotations/capabilities for ambiguous Arrow mappings, particularly TUPLE and VARIANT

Verify actual import/export at the selected engine pin. Define nested round trips, missing versus NULL, numeric/time identity, and SDK metadata preservation. Reject opaque aggregate-state layouts unless a portable state contract is proven.

optimizer.title: Optimizer and observability additions — design required
scope: Projection expressions and result mapping, repeatability, typed metrics, and any necessary partition-selection/parallelism additions

Reuse Filter v2 and existing split/partition/ordering metadata first. Define decline and local residual behavior, type/NULL semantics, query-scoped repeatability, metric units/lifetime, and selected-partition identity. Existing monotonicity and runtime-filter fields are not new additions.

sequences_types.title: Sequences and user-defined types
scope: Define discovery/create/alter/drop, sequence allocation/concurrency/rollback rules, and portable enum/type definitions. Separate transferable metadata from engine constructor callbacks.

collations_coordinates.title: Collations and coordinate systems
scope: Determine which descriptions can be shared and which execution semantics require engine-local implementation; qualify equality/order behavior before advertising a collation.

windows.title: Standalone window functions
scope: Inventory 2.0 registration and execution separately from existing aggregate-window support; establish whether a portable request/lifecycle can be included now.

statements.title: Raw SQL CONNECT and statement execution
scope: Review alongside read-query preparation, but specify writes/DDL, session state, result kinds, transaction effects, and retry rules separately. The read-query contract does not imply these capabilities.

multi_input.title: Multiple relational inputs
scope: Review the [existing engine proposal](multi_input_table_functions.md) for per-input identity/schema, ordering, backpressure, completion, cancellation, and transaction semantics. Include a wire contract only after the execution model has a working feasibility test.

cleanup.title: Existing protocol cleanup
scope: Review inconsistent names/types, scalar default-schema absence, duplicate operations, and weak metadata conventions together. Decide whether a clean major change is preferable to parallel legacy/new forms. Nested default search paths are not an upstream capability at the current pin.

scope: Raw paths, nested ownership, nullable default schema, complete metadata/result cache identity and dependency invalidation. Never split a SQL rendering.

Typed macro parameters need a semantic mapping. Wire `arguments_schema` currently describes parameter/default types and docs; qualify that it can express the desired declared-type contract.
Wire has SQL `definition`; preserve owner-relative name resolution, overload selection, and dependencies.
Native creation rejected; no sequence lifecycle/state RPC. A sequence feature needs allocation, concurrency, rollback policy, and metadata semantics, not just numeric field transport.

Native creation rejected. 2.0 constructor representation differs from 1.5 bind-function registration. User type/enum creation and discovery require an explicit contract; opaque C++ constructor callbacks cannot simply cross the wire.
Native creation rejected. Collation execution and comparison semantics need engine-local integration; no generic callback serialization.
No VGI creation/discovery integration. This structure already exists in the 1.5 baseline; it is not solely a new 2.0 gap.
Native schema creation hooks reject. Existing extension registration and worker function discovery are separate supported paths; port their callbacks in the function/COPY workstream.
Define identity, replacement, persistence, and dependencies.
Resolve full table ownership, including nested schema paths.
Implement the advertised before/after behavior and failure ordering.
Select the correct write events; qualify INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE and any combined write plans.
Preserve UPDATE OF column filtering; typed names must resolve to the target table.
Preserve row versus statement execution count.
Bind transition-table names to the correct NEW/OLD data.
Preserve query semantics and dependencies; establish execution location, transaction scope, and recursion policy.
2.0 `Identifier`; engine attachment alias. Keep distinct from the remote catalog name in `path`.
VGI interprets it as remote catalog selection/connection input. Preserve existing parsing, redaction, and cache identity.
New expression form; engine binds it into the path. Qualify prepared/dynamic attach rather than sending an AST to the worker.
Engine binds expressions into values; VGI consumes extension options and validates/forwards declared worker options. Preserve typed values and secret handling through the signature port.
Engine manages attachment conflicts. Test IF NOT EXISTS/REPLACE and resource cleanup; do not substitute table-create conflict handling.

New engine resource path. Provisioning/borrowing is handled before attachment, which receives the applied endpoint/options. Not automatically a missing catalog RPC. Qualify resource output compatibility with VGI LOCATION/catalog selection.
Engine binds parameters, provisions or borrows the provider, and owns teardown rules. Test failed attach, DETACH, and borrowed-resource lifetime; do not duplicate provider ownership in the worker.

Engine DatabaseManager renames the attachment. No remote catalog rename RPC is inherently needed. Qualify VGI cached names, published global functions, owner-qualified definitions, companion attachments, and detach cleanup.
Explicit opt-in. Leave disabled until multiple writes, failure/rollback, and RETURNING share correct worker transaction state. It does not enable ADD COLUMN's rewritten operations by itself.
IS_REMOTE, EXECUTE_QUERY_NODE, EXECUTE_STATEMENT, CONNECT are separate capabilities. VGI has no target implementations; define a SQL-capable worker profile if desired.
New optional execution integration, distinct from ordinary catalog metadata RPCs. Do not claim CONNECT or general SQL delegation merely because table scans work.
Existing requests carry the transaction token. Qualify transaction lifetime across create/alter/drop, CTAS, expanded ALTER, nested writes, and retries. Presence of a token is not proof of rollback.
